title: Investigation of Lamotrigine Crystal Polymorphs Using Crystal Structure Prediction and Terahertz Spectroscopy
abstract: Abstract Crystal structure prediction (CSP) plays a significant role in exploring the crystal polymorphism of pharmaceutical solids. Determination of the atomic-level structures of crystalline materials is a fundamental step in understanding their bulk physical and chemical properties and behavior in drug products. CSP can be performed using numerous computational approaches, but all ultimately require comparison with experimental measurements to confirm the CSP findings. In this work, terahertz (THz) vibrational spectroscopy is combined with powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) to demonstrate a new metrics framework for the validation of CSP investigations. Terahertz spectroscopy probes the low-frequency (≤150 cm−1) lattice vibrations of molecular crystals and provides a polymorph specific spectral profile that complements diffraction methods. This methodology is applied to the anti-epileptic drug lamotrigine, the subject of multiple crystal engineering studies to improve its formulated performance. A CSP search was performed on lamotrigine starting with a fast molecular mechanics survey for initial crystal structure candidates (∼800,000 structures), followed by high-accuracy solid-sta

summary: Introduces a combined terahertz spectroscopy–PXRD validation framework for CSP, applying it to lamotrigine to benchmark predicted polymorphs against experimental low-frequency lattice vibrations.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Crystal Structural Prototypes: Construction, Classification, and Applications
abstract: Crystal structural prototypes describe recurring atomic arrangements across chemically distinct materials. Prototype libraries are built through crystallographic curation, standardization, geometric matching, local-environment clustering, and periodic-graph analysis, and support chemical substitution, derivative enumeration, high-throughput screening, structure solution, crystal structure prediction (CSP), and generative design. This survey compares methods by the structural information they retain and the equivalence rules they impose, distinguishing crystallographic structure types, geometric realizations, chemistry-anonymous topologies, and chemical decorations. We review curated and automatically extracted prototype libraries (AFLOW, CSPD, LAE-ICSPD, EMFDTW, TYPIX, ICSD structure types), their source databases, and algorithms for assigning family membership. A GraphID-based analysis of samples from ICSD, the Materials Project, OQMD, and LeMat shows that the 100 most frequent families in each sample cover 30 to 67 percent of analyzed structures, while 72 to 82 percent of observed families are singletons. The GraphIDs of up to 76 percent of structures change when the neighbor tol

screen.reason: Prototype libraries & topology-based structure classification enable CSP candidate generation & ranking.

summary: Unifies and benchmarks crystal prototype construction methods using a GraphID-based analysis across ICSD, Materials Project, OQMD, and LeMat, quantifying family frequency skew and neighbor-tolerance sensitivity in prototype assignment.

title: A MACE interatomic potential for two dimensional and curved sp2 carbon: family level transfer benchmarks and a SOAP based structural novelty map

screen.reason: MACE MLIP development with transfer-learning benchmarks; directly applicable to molecular CSP acceleration.

summary: A MACE-based machine-learned interatomic potential for sp2 carbon is benchmarked across 2D and curved allotrope families using a SOAP-derived structural novelty map to quantify extrapolation risk beyond training data.

title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
abstract: Developing a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) that is accurate for the specific conditions under which it will be applied, rather than simply for the predefined configurations chosen by the model developer, is a significant challenge in atomistic simulation. Active learning (AL) addresses this challenge by closing the loop between candidate generation, data selection, reference calculation, and model updating. Here, we survey more than seventy studies, with an emphasis on work from 2020 to 2026, to understand how active learning has evolved from a niche, on-the-fly training technique for query-by-committee and Gaussian process force fields into a diverse family of data-efficient strategies. he reviewed examples include on-the-fly molecular dynamics, active data selection for fine-tuning pretrained models, kernel- and representation-based acquisition using frozen pretrained models, and reaction-aware sampling for chemical systems far from equilibrium. We explore the use of active learning in elemental and alloy mechanics, hydrogen and ion diffusion, ferroelectrics and effective Hamiltonians of functional materials, reactive and photochemical dynamics, high-entropy and c

screen.reason: Active learning for MLIPs directly accelerates CSP workflows; uncertainty-driven sampling crucial for polymorph ranking.

summary: Synthesizes 70+ active-learning MLIP studies into a unified taxonomy spanning on-the-fly, fine-tuning, and frozen-representation acquisition strategies, clarifying how uncertainty-driven data efficiency has evolved since 2020.

title: All-electron machine-learned orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems
abstract: We introduce STRUCTURES-P, a machine-learned all-electron orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems. Electrostatics are evaluated analytically in an atom-centered Gaussian basis, while an equivariant network learns the kinetic and exchange-correlation energy from energies and gradients of non-ground-state densities. Minimizing the functional from a superposition of atomic densities recovers the Kohn-Sham ground state: on held-out crystals, the density error falls from 6.7% to 0.4% of the electron count and the energy error reaches 0.25 mHa per atom, half that of a same-architecture interatomic potential. A single functional can be trained for both isolated molecules and periodic systems, and the model generalizes to larger unit cells. It largely preserves relative-energy rankings and reproduces convex-hull vertices on the tested H-N composition slice. Together, these results demonstrate the viability of machine-learned all-electron orbital-free DFT for variational density optimization and energy evaluation in fixed-geometry solids.

screen.reason: ML orbital-free DFT for periodic CHNO systems; potential MLIP alternative for CSP energy ranking, but unfixed-geometry v

summary: Introduces STRUCTURES-P, an equivariant machine-learned all-electron orbital-free density functional (analytic electrostatics plus learned kinetic/XC energy) enabling accurate periodic CHNO density optimization and energy ranking without pseudopotentials

title: Accuracy of Vibrational Properties of Machine-Learning Force Fields for Molecular Crystal Transformations
abstract: Machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) enable the calculation of transformation pathways in molecular crystals at a fraction of the computational cost of density functional theory (DFT). However, a good agreement in energies and structures does not necessarily imply an accurate description of vibrational properties, which are essential for characterizing transition states and determining free energies at finite temperatures. Herein, we assess the accuracy of system-specific SO3krates MLFFs trained on PBE+MBD reference data for describing vibrational properties of molecular crystal transformations. As examples, we consider a polymorph transition of 1,4-diiodobenzene and a single-crystal-to-single-crystal Diels-Alder reaction. The transition state structures obtained from solid-state nudged-elastic-band (NEB) calculations with the MLFFs exhibit a single imaginary $Γ$-point frequency associated with the respective transformation. Compared with PBE+MBD, the mean absolute errors of $Γ$-point vibrational frequencies and relative harmonic free energies at 300 K are about 3 cm$^{-1}$ and 1 kJ/mol, respectively. Furthermore, we compare for the Diels-Alder reaction a collective transformation

screen.reason: MLFFs for molecular crystal transformations, vibrational accuracy assessment for polymorph transitions.

summary: Benchmarks SO3krates MLFFs against PBE+MBD for molecular-crystal transition states, showing ~3 cm⁻¹ frequency and ~1 kJ/mol free-energy errors across polymorph and Diels–Alder NEB pathways.

title: Targeted fine-tuning of machine-learning interatomic potentials for phonons and phase transitions
abstract: Abstract Machine-learning interatomic potentials are widely used as computationally efficient surrogates for density functional theory in atomistic simulations, enabling large-scale and long-time modeling of materials systems. Here, we investigate how different fine-tuning strategies affect the prediction of harmonic phonon band structures, thermal and elastic properties, and the potential-energy surface along unstable phonon modes. We show that substantial improvements can be achieved with very limited additional data, with as few as 10 material-specific training structures. We investigate targeted L 2 -SP ( L 2 -TSP) for this application, combining regularization toward the pre-trained model with selective fine-tuning of the first two representation-building layers, alongside transfer learning and multihead fine-tuning, with an additional comparison to low-rank LoRA for phonon prediction. Across 53 materials, L 2 -TSP achieves the most consistent overall performance, reducing phonon errors while also improving predictions of thermodynamic and elastic properties. Importantly, models with similar harmonic phonon accuracy can differ substantially in their prediction of dynamical ins

screen.reason: MLIP fine-tuning for phonons/phase transitions; transfer learning methodology applicable to CSP lattice-energy ranking.

summary: Introduces targeted L2-SP fine-tuning (regularized, selective updates to early representation layers) of pretrained MLIPs, outperforming transfer learning, multihead, and LoRA for phonon and phase-transition prediction across 53 materials.

title: Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials
abstract: The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations, this noise is challenging to identify. Existing mitigation strategies, such as manual filtering or iterative refinement of outliers, require either substantial expert effort or multiple expensive retraining cycles, making them difficult to scale to large datasets. Here, we introduce a noise-resilient training method that automatically down-weighs noisy samples, without requiring additional reference calculations. By tracking the loss distribution via an exponential moving average, this unsupervised method identifies outliers throughout a single training run. We show that this approach prevents overfitting and matches the performance of iterative refinement baselines with significantly reduced overhead. The method’s effectiveness is demonstrated by recovering accurate physical observables for liquid water from unconverged reference data, including diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, we validate its scalability by training a foundation model for organic chemistry on the SPICE dataset, w

screen.reason: MLIP training robustness directly applicable to CSP reference-data generation; scalable noise-handling enables larger CS

summary: Introduces an unsupervised, single-pass training method that down-weights noisy samples via an exponential moving average of per-sample loss, avoiding costly iterative retraining for MLIP datasets.

title: Architecture-agnostic knowledge distillation for machine-learning interatomic potentials

screen.reason: MLIP knowledge distillation novel method; direct transfer to accelerating CSP searches

summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictive accuracy from large, high-cost machine-learning interatomic potentials to smaller, architecture-different student models regardless of network design, enabling faster CSP-relevant energy/force evaluations without retraining from scratch.

title: Understanding compression-extension error asymmetry in universal machine-learning interatomic potentials
abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials are increasingly used across diverse materials, yet their reliability under directional deformation remains unclear. We compare compression and extension along paired deformation paths from the same parent structures for eleven pretrained potentials. The benchmark comprises 1,963 Materials Project trajectory (MPtrj) parents and 1,286 experimental-source MinX-Eq parents at six strain magnitudes from 1% to 10%. Density-functional theory provides references for isotropic, uniaxial and biaxial loading in MPtrj and isotropic loading in MinX-Eq. At $\pm 10\%$, every model has a larger median force error under compression, with pooled isotropic compression-to-extension ratios of 2.12 and 3.30 for MPtrj and MinX-Eq. Decomposing error growth into DFT force-scale growth and relative-error evolution shows that relative errors decrease on both branches, faster under compression in MPtrj but slower under compression in MinX-Eq. Force-scale matching moves the error ratios toward unity, although MinX-Eq retains a compression-side excess across models. Radial and SOAP analyses place compressed structures at shorter separations and farther from publ

screen.reason: MLIP benchmark revealing directional-deformation asymmetry; informs potential selection/training for CSP lattice-energy

summary: Introduces a paired compression/extension benchmark (MPtrj and MinX-Eq, 1%-10% strains) quantifying and decomposing universal ML potentials' systematic compression-side force-error excess via force-scale and SOAP/radial analysis.

title: HIP: Hessian Interatomic Potentials without derivatives

screen.reason: Novel MLIP training avoiding derivatives; direct potential for accelerating MCSP lattice-energy ranking.

summary: A Hessian-free interatomic potential architecture that directly predicts energy-conserving force fields without backpropagating through derivatives, likely cutting training and inference cost versus gradient-based MLIPs.

title: Linear response for machine-learned interatomic potentials: phonons at arbitrary wave vectors from the primitive cell
abstract: Phonon calculations with machine-learned interatomic potentials are almost exclusively performed with finite displacements in supercells, an approach that is exact only at wave vectors commensurate with the supercell and whose error depends on the range of the force constants. In message-passing networks this range grows with the number of layers, and reaches 140 angstrom for the deepest universal models. Here we show that the dynamical matrix of a message-passing potential can be obtained exactly in the primitive cell, at any wave vector, as the linear response of the forces to a displacement modulated by a Bloch phase, in the spirit of density-functional perturbation theory. The phase enters only where the features of neighboring atoms are gathered, and the trained model is used without modification. One further derivative yields group velocities and mode Grüneisen parameters analytically. We apply the method to NequIP and Prophet, and reproduce the Hessians of supercells to machine precision. Using these results as a reference, we find that the supercells commonly employed in high-throughput calculations lead to errors of several tenths of a THz in the phonon frequencies, and th

screen.reason: MLIP phonon methodology improves CSP lattice-energy ranking; transfer-ready but not direct molecular-CSP.

summary: Introduces a Bloch-phase linear-response scheme enabling exact, arbitrary-wavevector phonon dynamical matrices (plus group velocities, Grüneisen parameters) directly from the primitive cell for message-passing interatomic potentials, avoiding sup

title: Pressure-transferable universal machine-learning potentials: the WBM-MatPES benchmark and Tuga-FF
abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials hold the promise to replace costly ab initio calculations in materials science workflows. However, the accuracy and transferability of current models are limited by the availability of training data. We release WBM-MatPES, a dataset of 182 thousand structures recomputed with consistent MatPES settings, together with two reference convex hulls of different depths and test sets at six pressures up to 150 GPa. These datasets reproduce a realistic discovery workflow and allow potentials to be ranked systematically at this level of theory, similar to the Matbench Discovery leaderboard at the Materials Project settings. In this benchmark, five published MatPES potentials agree within 12 meV/atom at 25 GPa, yet their errors increase dramatically to 0.4-5 eV/atom at 150 GPa. To address this limitation, we develop Tuga-FF, a graph transformer trained on datasets spanning ambient and high-pressure configurations alike. Tuga-FF is the most accurate model in the benchmark at ambient pressure, with an energy error of 13.6 meV/atom, and maintains an error of just 21 meV/atom at 150 GPa. We believe this benchmark will encourage the community to tr

screen.reason: MLIP benchmark and high-pressure transferability relevant to CSP ranking, but inorganic-focused.

summary: Introduces WBM-MatPES, a multi-pressure (up to 150 GPa) convex-hull benchmark dataset plus Tuga-FF, a graph-transformer potential achieving stable accuracy across pressures where existing MatPES models fail.

title: Challenging Atomistic Foundation Models on Disordered Carbons
abstract: Foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise broad transferability, yet their out-of-domain reliability is hard to establish. Here, we use pure and O/H-containing disordered carbon spanning multiple phases, competing hybridisations and porous frameworks to stress-test six popular foundation MLIPs. We first screen all six on density functional theory (DFT) energy and force errors and binding curves, then subject four to melt-quench-anneal molecular dynamics and evaluate the resulting structural observables. Binding curves and O/H-containing trajectories reveal unphysical extrapolation and dynamical failures that low DFT energy and force errors fail to reveal. Of the models tested, MACE-MH-1 is the most consistently robust, with low DFT errors and stable MD. Despite differing architectures, OMAT-based models share structural biases, highlighting the importance of training coverage. All four models generate structures of nanoporous carbon that reproduce the principal experimental and specialised carbon potential signatures. Incorporating O/H leaves short-range order largely unchanged but shifts pore-size distributions towards larger pores. These results emphasise

screen.reason: MLIP benchmarking with MD validation; transferability stress-test relevant to CSP reliability.

summary: Introduces a disordered-carbon (pure and O/H-doped) stress-test benchmark combining DFT error screens with melt-quench-anneal MD, revealing that low energy/force errors mask unphysical extrapolation and dynamical failures across six foundation MLIP

title: Hierarchical universal open structure dataset for atomistic modeling
abstract: Atomic-scale simulations have been transformed by machine-learning models that predict the properties of atomistic structures with the accuracy of quantum calculations, but at a small fraction of the cost. These models have increased dramatically in generality, thanks to the availability of synthetic datasets of ever-increasing size and scope. The proliferation of datasets, with properties often computed using different levels of electronic-structure approximation, is problematic, as there is often overlap between different datasets, and strong correlations between structures obtained with short molecular dynamics trajectories or geometry optimization. To address these problems, we introduce a protocol to stratify a dataset into a hierarchy of nested subsets, subsampling from the coarsest to the finest resolution based on an "ecumetric" built to reflect the latent space representation of several popular universal machine-learning interatomic potentials. We then use this approach to combine most of the open structural datasets currently available, consolidating them into MAD-COSMO, a well-organized collection of almost 1.7 billion structures, whose $2^{24}$ most diverse members form

screen.reason: Large-scale diverse atomic structure dataset; enables MLIP training for CSP applications.

summary: Introduces an "ecumetric"-based hierarchical subsampling protocol to merge heterogeneous open atomistic datasets into MAD-COSMO, a deduplicated, diversity-stratified corpus of ~1.7 billion structures.

title: Risk-Controlled DFT Selection for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Automated materials discovery requires evaluating large pools of candidate configurations, with density functional theory (DFT) as a major throughput bottleneck. Pretrained machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approximate DFT cheaply, but their errors vary by orders of magnitude across configurations, making it difficult to decide when to trust the MLIP predictions and when to fall back to DFT. We frame this decision as a risk-controlled selection problem and solve it within a conformal risk control (CRC) framework. Each configuration is mapped from atomic numbers and Cartesian coordinates to a fixed geometric descriptor, which a lightweight predictor uses to estimate an MLIP-DFT disagreement score in energy, average force, and maximum force. CRC then calibrates this score into a selection threshold for DFT labeling such that the MLIP error on the unselected configurations, which keep their MLIP labels, stays below a user-chosen fraction $α$ of the expected error. Under an identical guarantee across eight dataset-MLIP pairs, our predictor routes 7% and 14% fewer configurations to DFT at $α=0.3$ than committee baselines. Because committee disagreement overlooks errors the

screen.reason: MLIP-DFT selection framework directly applicable to CSP screening bottleneck; novel risk-control approach.

summary: Introduces a conformal-risk-control framework that calibrates a lightweight descriptor-based disagreement predictor into a DFT-selection threshold, cutting DFT calls 7–14% versus committee baselines while guaranteeing bounded MLIP error.

title: LunaTP: Enabling Efficient and Scalable Tensor Product for Equivariant MLIPs
abstract: Equivariant machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise atomistic simulations with accuracy approaching that of quantum-mechanical calculations. However, the high computational cost of their core Clebsch--Gordan tensor product (CGTP) convolutions severely limits model scalability and efficiency. In this paper, we rethink the parallel execution of CGTP convolutions and introduce LunaTP. Built on node-centric execution, LunaTP exploits path-group parallelism and multi-level reuse to accelerate CGTP convolutions and higher-order derivative computation while preserving the underlying mathematical formulation. On an NVIDIA H100 GPU, LunaTP achieves kernel speedups of up to 250.0$\times$ over e3nn and 17.1$\times$ over OpenEquivariance. It also delivers end-to-end training throughput gains of up to 28.7$\times$ over e3nn and 3.11$\times$ over OpenEquivariance. Finally, LunaTP demonstrates scalability and robust performance across models, workload scales, and GPUs, delivering substantial acceleration for training and atomistic simulation with high-accuracy equivariant MLIPs.

screen.reason: MLIP acceleration directly enables CSP lattice-energy ranking; strong engineering but limited algorithmic novelty.

summary: LunaTP introduces path-group parallelism and multi-level reuse for node-centric Clebsch–Gordan tensor product execution, delivering up to 250× kernel and 28.7× end-to-end training speedups for equivariant MLIPs.

title: On the Theoretical Limits of Learning Unconstrained Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) accelerate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations by learning the energies and forces that govern atomic motion. Recent work has shown that relaxing physical inductive biases can improve computational efficiency and predictive accuracy, raising the question of whether energy-and-force matching alone is sufficient to ensure accurate sampling. We show that, for unconstrained hypothesis classes, the relationship between prediction error and sampling accuracy is exponentially ill-conditioned in dimension. In particular, prediction errors that decay exponentially with dimension can coexist with nearly maximal total variation distance between the learned and target distributions. We identify two failure mechanisms. The first is kinetic trapping, where relaxation to an accurate learned equilibrium requires exponentially long times, even when simulations are initialized from training configurations at which energies and forces are matched exactly. The second is equilibrium mismatch, where the learned stationary distribution itself remains far from the target. Under explicit assumptions, we show that equilibrium mismatch can persist even in local,

screen.reason: MLIP theory for MD sampling; identifies fundamental limits of unconstrained potentials relevant to CSP relaxation.

summary: Establishes theoretical bounds showing unconstrained MLIPs can have exponentially small energy/force errors yet produce exponentially wrong equilibrium sampling, identifying kinetic trapping and equilibrium mismatch as distinct failure modes.

title: Symbolic ensemble learning enables discovery of fast accurate physics-based interatomic potentials

screen.reason: Novel MLIP discovery method; direct potential for accelerating CSP energy ranking.

summary: Introduces a symbolic-regression ensemble-learning framework to automatically discover fast, physically interpretable interatomic potentials, rather than relying on fixed functional forms or black-box machine-learning models.
